parsed_output.evidence: Root cause / sink: IOUtils.java, method unzip(String,String) — specifically line 124 `File destFile = new File(newPath, currentEntry);` where `currentEntry = entry.getName()` (line 122) is the untrusted ZipEntry name coming straight from the archive's central directory, and line 126/129 `destFile.getParentFile().mkdirs()` which creates arbitrary parent directories derived from that untrusted path before any write occurs. Trust boundary crossed: the zip archive is attacker-controlled input (uploaded plugin/agent bundle or any file handed to IOUtils.unzip), while `extractFolder` is the caller-configured, supposedly-trusted destination root — no check ever verifies the resolved `destFile`/`destinationParent` stays inside `extractFolder` before mkdirs()/FileOutputStream. Ran the PoV against the built (unpatched) module: it printed `escaped=true` and exited 0, i.e., `../pov_zipslip_proof.txt` landed one directory above the extraction root. I also hand-patched a copy of IOUtils.java to canonicalize and reject out-of-root paths and reran the same PoV byte-for-byte against those patched classes: it exited 1 with `escaped=false` and an explicit rejection exception, confirming the test discriminates vulnerable vs. patched behavior. There is a single vulnerability entry in the alert with one trace, and within that trace there are effectively two sink operations sharing the same unvalidated `destFile`/`destinationParent` root cause that a complete fix must cover: (1) line 126/129 `destinationParent.mkdirs()` — arbitrary directory creation outside the destination root, and (2) line 141 `new FileOutputStream(destFile)` — arbitrary file write/overwrite outside the destination root using the same tainted `destFile`. Both must be fixed together since they derive from the same unchecked path.
parsed_output.expected_vulnerable_behavior: IOUtils.unzip() writes the marker file at basedir/pov_zipslip_proof.txt (sibling of, i.e. one level above, the extraction directory basedir/extract) instead of confining it under the extraction directory, because it resolves the destination purely from `new File(extractFolder, entry.getName())` and eagerly mkdirs() the resulting parent without any containment check. The PoV detects this by checking file existence outside the extraction dir and exits 0 in that case.
parsed_output.notes: Alert contains one vulnerability with one trace (lines 122→124→126→129 in IOUtils.java), pointing at the classic Zip Slip pattern: untrusted `entry.getName()` flows into `new File(newPath, currentEntry)` and then into `destinationParent.mkdirs()`. I targeted this exact trace directly by calling the real public `IOUtils.unzip(String, String)` API with a crafted `../pov_zipslip_proof.txt` entry — no simulation, no bypassing of project code. I additionally flagged the sibling sink at line 141 (`new FileOutputStream(destFile)`) in `evidence`/`regression_hint` because it consumes the same unvalidated `destFile` computed at line 124 and must be covered by the same fix (a containment check placed before line 129 covers both the mkdirs and the later write, but a fix that only special-cases the mkdirs call and forgets the FileOutputStream write — or vice versa — would still leave a bypass). Verified empirically both that the PoV exits 0 today (unpatched) and exits 1 against a canonicalize-and-reject patch, so the command is a valid pass/fail regression gate for a downstream patch.

parsed_output.regression_hint: Invariant: for every ZipEntry processed in IOUtils.unzip(), the resolved destination file path (after resolving `..`, `.`, symlinks, and OS-specific separators) must be a descendant of (or exactly equal to) the canonical extraction root; if it is not, unzip must reject/skip that entry (throw or continue) before performing any filesystem mutation — neither `destinationParent.mkdirs()` (line 129) nor `new FileOutputStream(destFile)` (line 141) may execute against a path outside the root. A correct fix should validate using canonical paths (e.g., `File.getCanonicalPath()` / `Path.normalize()` plus a `startsWith(root + separator)` check, or `Path.relativize`/`Path.startsWith` on normalized paths) rather than naive string checks, and must apply to both the directory-creation call site and the file-write call site since they share the same tainted `destFile`. Known bypass variants the fix must also block: (a) simple `../` traversal (as used in this PoV) and multi-level `../../../etc/...`; (b) absolute-path entry names (e.g. `/etc/cron.d/evil` or `C:\\...` on Windows) that ignore `extractFolder` entirely when passed to `new File(base, absoluteChild)`; (c) mixed/alternate separators (`..\\`) on platforms where both separators are honored; (d) traversal hidden inside a directory-entry name (`entry.isDirectory()` true) that still reaches `destinationParent.mkdirs()` before the file-write guard would even run; (e) symlink-based escapes where a legitimately-named entry writes through a pre-existing symlink inside the extraction root that points outside it (canonicalization/realpath check handles this too). Any regression test suite should include at least: `../evil.txt`, `../../evil.txt`, `/tmp/evil.txt` (absolute), and a directory-only entry named `../evildir/`.
parsed_output.summary: Created a PoV (ZipSlipPoV.java) that exercises the real com.alibaba.oneagent.utils.IOUtils.unzip(String, String) API with a malicious zip entry named "../pov_zipslip_proof.txt". On the current code, unzip() blindly resolves `new File(newPath, currentEntry)` and `mkdirs()`s the parent, letting the entry write a file one directory above the intended extraction folder — confirmed by running the compiled PoV against the built classes (marker file escaped, exit 0). Against a locally patched version of IOUtils.java that canonicalizes and validates destFile stays under the extraction root, unzip() throws and the PoV exits 1, proving the test discriminates correctly.

parsed_output.patch_notes: In IOUtils.unzip(String, String): compute destDirCanonicalPath = new File(extractFolder).getCanonicalPath() once. For each ZipEntry, after building destFile = new File(newPath, currentEntry), compute destFile.getCanonicalPath() and verify it equals destDirCanonicalPath or starts with destDirCanonicalPath + File.separator; otherwise throw IOException("Zip entry is outside of the target dir: " + currentEntry) before calling destinationParent.mkdirs() or opening the FileOutputStream. This check runs for every entry (files and directories alike) so directory-only traversal entries are also blocked before mkdirs(). Added IOUtilsUnzipTest.java with JUnit 4 tests: rejects "../pov_zipslip_proof.txt", rejects nested "../../evil.txt", rejects a directory-only traversal entry "../evildir/", and confirms a normal nested entry ("safe/nested/file.txt") still extracts correctly.
parsed_output.risk_notes: Low risk: the change only adds a containment check before existing filesystem operations; it does not alter behavior for well-formed archives whose entries stay within the extraction root (verified via a passing "still extracts normal entries" test and the full existing module test suite, 9/9 passing). getCanonicalPath() can throw IOException on some platforms/filesystem edge cases (e.g. broken symlinks) — this is already declared by unzip()'s throws clause so no new checked-exception surface is introduced. Absolute-path zip entries were analyzed and, per java.io.UnixFileSystem's resolve() semantics (parent+child concatenation, not replacement), remain naturally contained under the extraction root on this JDK/OS combination, and are additionally covered by the canonical-path check regardless. Symlink-based escapes are also mitigated since getCanonicalPath() resolves symlinks before the comparison.
parsed_output.summary: Fixed a Zip Slip / path traversal vulnerability (CWE-22) in IOUtils.unzip(). Untrusted ZipEntry names were used to build destFile via new File(newPath, currentEntry) without any containment check, allowing entries like "../pov_zipslip_proof.txt" to create directories (destinationParent.mkdirs()) and write files (new FileOutputStream(destFile)) outside the intended extraction folder. The fix canonicalizes the extraction root once and, for every entry, canonicalizes the resolved destFile and rejects (throws IOException) any entry whose canonical path is not equal to or a descendant of the canonical extraction root — before any mkdirs() or file write occurs. This single check at the shared trust boundary covers both sink operations (parent directory creation and file write) and blocks the standard bypass variants (simple/nested "../" traversal, directory-only traversal entries) since it operates on the fully resolved/normalized path rather than naive string matching.

parsed_output.summary: The patch fixes the CWE-22 zip-slip vulnerability in IOUtils.unzip() by canonicalizing the extraction root once and, for every zip entry, canonicalizing the resolved destFile and rejecting (throwing IOException) any entry whose canonical path is not the root or a descendant of it, before destinationParent.mkdirs() or the FileOutputStream write occurs. This directly addresses both sink operations named in the alert trace (parent-dir creation at line ~140 and file write at line ~152) using a robust canonical-path containment check rather than naive string matching, which also covers directory-only traversal entries and symlink-based escapes. A new JUnit test file (IOUtilsUnzipTest.java) was added covering simple traversal, nested traversal, directory-entry traversal, and a normal-extraction regression case.
